title: Why great candidates disappear during interviews
summary: Strong candidates rarely get rejected. They slip away when a process goes quiet. Here's where it happens and how to move faster.
body_markdown:
A founder meets an engineer on Monday. The call goes well, everyone agrees on a next step, and then the week fills up: a fundraise update, a customer fire, a release. By the time anyone follows up, the engineer has two other processes moving, and one of them has already made an offer.


Nobody decided to pass on that candidate. The process just went quiet at the wrong moment. On Contrario, the typical hire closes about a month after the company first meets the candidate. The median is 30 days for full-stack engineers and 28 for forward deployed engineers, a role whose share of requests has roughly tripled in six months. A quarter of full-stack hires close within 20 days. The strongest candidates move on that timeline, and they don't wait for a process that falls behind it.


They slip away in three places.
